app.title: Jidō Kundoku
app.tagline: Classical Chinese, read as Japanese. Paste a passage and get it marked up for reading aloud, with a plain Japanese version alongside.
sidebar.uploadHint: Skips in-browser parsing; annotates a pre-parsed SUD tree directly.
main.empty: Enter text or upload a CoNLL-U file to begin.

help.title: Editing the analysis
help.intro: Every character is analysed for its part of speech and for which other character it depends on. That analysis drives the reading order, the kaeriten and the plain-Japanese version — so correcting it corrects all three. The examples below are live: they follow your theme and language, just as the app does.
help.step.select.title: Select a character
help.step.select.body: Click any character. Its part of speech appears beside it, and an arrow is drawn from the character it depends on, labelled with the relation between them. Click it again, or press Escape, to deselect. The arrow keys move to the next character or line.
help.step.pos.title: Change the part of speech
help.step.pos.body: Right-click the part-of-speech label to choose another. The current one is marked. Both panels redraw immediately, since the reading depends on this: 中 as a verb is read あたル, as a noun なか.
help.step.relation.title: Change the relation
help.step.relation.body: Right-click the label on the arrow to choose a different relation. This is what decides whether a character is read before the one it depends on — and so whether it needs a kaeriten at all.
help.step.head.title: Attach it to a different character
help.step.head.body: Drag a character onto the one it should depend on. A dashed line follows the pointer and the target highlights as you pass over it. Once dropped, the relation is relabelled by the parser itself, scoring the new arrow the way it scored the original analysis.
help.step.root.title: Make a character the main predicate
help.step.root.body: Choose 文の主辞 from the relation menu. A sentence has exactly one main predicate, so everything that depended on the old one is carried across to the new one and relabelled to suit.
help.step.reading.title: Choose a different reading
help.step.reading.body: Right-click the furigana for that character's other readings, listed on'yomi first and limited to those its part of speech allows. Readings are shown in historical kana, as on the page.
help.step.undo.title: Undo anything
help.step.undo.body: Every edit can be undone, including a change that moved several characters at once. Add Shift to redo. Your edits travel with the text when you save it or download it as CoNLL-U.
